official.deadline_note: The SMU Merit Scholarship publishes no separate scholarship deadline. SMU states there is no need to apply for the scholarship separately, and that scholarship eligibility is considered automatically as part of the admissions application, so the deadline is the admissions deadline for the intake. The SMU Merit Scholarship page and its Singapore Citizens scholarship overview page publish no dated window for any intake, and the AY2026-2027 admission cycle referenced in the catalogue (16 March 2026 to 19 March 2026) has passed.

applicant_utility.summary: This award covers the full tuition fee, including the 10% Ministry of Education grant administration fees, for the entire duration of your SMU degree, plus a Growth Opportunities allowance that pays for overseas exchanges, approved summer programmes, study missions and community service projects - but there is no living stipend, so you still need to fund food and rent yourself. It is only for Singapore Citizens and Singapore Permanent Residents, and you must apply in your first year of study. There is no application form: SMU shortlists from your admissions application, then asks shortlisted candidates for a video presentation and an interview.
applicant_utility.best_fit: Singapore Citizens and Singapore Permanent Residents entering a full-time SMU undergraduate degree, particularly the Bachelor of Business Management, who can apply in their first year
application_readiness_checklist: Confirm Singapore Citizenship or Permanent Residency - the award is closed to internationals regardless of profile
Apply within your first year of study at SMU; the eligibility rules make later applications impossible
Note that you may apply for both the SMU Merit Scholarship and the SMU Global Impact Scholarship but can hold only one at a time
Prepare a video presentation in advance, because shortlisting happens without notice and the video is the next step
Plan to take the SMU Tuition Grant Scheme, as scholars must be on it and tuition coverage is conditional on continued grant eligibility
common_rejection_risks: Being outside the January 2026 or August 2026 cohort restriction that SMU published for this award, or being past your first year of study
Assuming a living allowance exists - there is none, so a funding plan built on the award alone will fail
Not being on the Tuition Grant Scheme, or losing grant eligibility, which voids the tuition coverage
Holding another SMU award simultaneously; scholars can hold only one scholarship at a time
Programme mismatch - the award is tied to the Bachelor of Business Management and the SMU Connexion double degree programme, and to Covenant Scholars and Double Degree Programme candidates
applicant_utility.estimated_uncovered_costs: Accommodation, meals, transport, books and personal expenses in Singapore, which the award does not cover beyond the S$3,000 support and the Growth Opportunities allowance, plus any global exposure programme cost above that allowance
document_audit: No document pack is published for the scholarship itself, so your admissions application is the whole file - make the academic and leadership evidence in it complete
Expect to produce a video presentation at shortlisting stage and prepare for an interview; there is no published format or prompt, so plan for a general personal-presentation pitch
alerts: SMU states explicitly that there is no need to apply for the scholarship separately - chasing an application form wastes time and may cause you to miss the actual automatic consideration
Tuition coverage lasts only while you remain eligible for the tuition grant, so a grant lapse ends the benefit
The cohort restriction to January 2026 or August 2026 may or may not be renewed for later intakes - verify the published criteria before relying on them
SMU's scholarship pages warn that the list of awards on its third-party highlights portal may not be current, and that scholarship terms may change; work only from admissions.smu.edu.sg
applicant_utility.submission_workflow: Submit the SMU admissions application for your intake, do not file a separate scholarship form, then wait for SMU to notify shortlisted candidates and complete the video presentation and interview

official.deadline_note: SIT publishes no dated application window on the Temasek Scholarship page. SIT's Bond-Free Scholarships page states that applications for Public Bursaries, Donated Bursaries and Scholarships commence in July, while the Temasek Scholarship page's own How To Apply text still reads 'July 2022' and the Bond-Free Scholarships index page reads 'July 2025'. Applicants are told to watch their SIT e-mail address for further information, which is sent to matriculated students, so there is no published deadline to record.
official.application_cycle: Annual post-matriculation application cycle administered by SIT; applications are stated to commence in July, with no published opening or closing date
official.status_note: SIT's award page is live with full benefit terms, and the Bond-Free Scholarships index page states applications commence in July and notices go out to matriculated students' SIT e-mail addresses. Because the award is applied for after matriculation rather than at admission, there is no admissions deadline to attach to it.

It is part of the S$150 million T-Spring community gift made by Temasek to mark its 50th anniversary in 2024.

verification.notes: Read SIT's own Temasek Scholarship page and its Bond-Free Scholarships index page on singaporetech.edu.sg, the administering institution. Confirmed the up-to-S$18,030 per annum value, the S$7,200 annual stipend, the S$2,000 one-time laptop allowance, the possible S$10,000 one-time Global Mobility Grant, the merit basis, the STEM and SIT degree restriction, the Singapore Citizens and Singapore Permanent Residents restriction, the T-Spring donor background, and the post-matriculation IN4SIT application route with an endorsed Letter of Recommendation and SIT Record of Achievement. applicant_utility.summary: This is worth up to S$18,030 a year with a S$7,200 stipend inside it, plus a one-off S$2,000 laptop allowance and a possible one-off S$10,000 Global Mobility Grant - but the single most important fact is that you do not apply for it at admission. You apply after you have matriculated at SIT, through the IN4SIT student intranet in the July cycle, so as an applicant you should apply to SIT first and treat this as a first-year opportunity. It is restricted to Singapore Citizens and Singapore Permanent Residents studying full-time STEM degrees, and you will need an endorsed Letter of Recommendation and your SIT Record of Achievement ready to upload.
applicant_utility.best_fit: Singapore Citizens and Singapore Permanent Residents enrolled in, or admitted to, a full-time STEM undergraduate degree at SIT who can apply after matriculation in the July cycle
application_readiness_checklist: Understand the route: apply to SIT first, matriculate, then apply for the scholarship through IN4SIT - it is not part of the admissions application
Watch your SIT e-mail address around July, since that is how SIT says the notice and further information reach students
Line up an endorser for your Letter of Recommendation early, since it must be endorsed and uploaded
Check your SIT Record of Achievement and start filling it well before the window opens
Confirm your degree is a full-time STEM programme at SIT, as the award is explicitly STEM-scoped
Plan your global exposure programme choice, since the S$10,000 Global Mobility Grant only applies if you are eligible for and choose to attend a University-conducted global exposure programme
common_rejection_risks: Being an international student - the award is restricted to Singapore Citizens and Singapore Permanent Residents
Applying at the admissions stage and never revisiting the award after matriculation, which is where the actual application happens
Enrolling in a non-STEM degree, or a part-time programme, which both fall outside the award's scope
Uploading an unendorsed Letter of Recommendation, or missing the SIT Record of Achievement where applicable
Assuming the laptop allowance and mobility grant are additive to the S$18,030 annual value - SIT does not state whether they sit inside or outside it
applicant_utility.estimated_uncovered_costs: Any tuition contribution not covered by the annual value, since SIT does not disclose the tuition element, and all general living costs in Singapore beyond the S$7,200 stipend
document_audit: The endorsed Letter of Recommendation is the item most likely to be missing at the deadline - agree the endorsement with your referee before the window opens
The SIT Record of Achievement is required where applicable, so check whether it applies to your year of study before assuming it is optional
Everything is uploaded through the SIT application portal rather than emailed, so scan and label documents in advance
alerts: SIT's own pages give conflicting years for the July start of applications - the award page says July 2022 and the Bond-Free Scholarships index says July 2025 - so confirm the current cycle with SIT rather than trusting either date
The Temasek Scholarship is bond-free, but it is one of SIT's donated bond-free scholarships, so read the linked Terms and Conditions before accepting
The Global Mobility Grant is conditional on being eligible for and choosing a University-conducted global exposure programme, so it is not guaranteed cash
SIT warns that its scholarship terms may change and that the Terms and Conditions page governs, so verify the value and conditions at the point of award
applicant_utility.submission_workflow: Matriculate at SIT on a full-time STEM degree, watch for the July application notice to your SIT e-mail address, then log in to IN4SIT, complete the online form and upload the endorsed Letter of Recommendation, Record of Achievement and any other supporting documents by the given deadline
